builds.title: Movement: reel in is a slingshot, not a brake (MV-0008)
builds.summary: MV-0008: reeling in (hold E) mid-swing now works like a slingshot instead of a brake. Reeling in a few metres at the bottom of a swing gives about 56% more total speed (35% more swing speed) than not reeling, and roughly double the carry when you let go (about 21 m versus 10 m); reeling on the upswing gives about +67% total speed. The pull now builds up over a fraction of a second instead of an instant jerk, and the swing no longer gets pinned under the anchor. Holding E for a long time (over about 0.6 s) still hauls you toward the anchor, so release early. The debug HUD (F1) now shows your total speed while you are hooked.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). Right mouse or Q fires and releases the grapple, hold E reels in, hold X reels out, Space releases. R respawns at the start with the view level, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Hook a beam or a tree branch, get a swing going, and at the bottom of the swing hold E for about half a second, then release the hook (Q or right mouse) a moment later. Do you shoot forward faster and carry much further than if you had not reeled? Try it again on the upswing. Does the pull feel smooth, not like a jerk or a brake? Press F1: does the HUD show your total speed while hooked? Is it too much or too little?

builds.title: Zeigote: M4 complete, day gathering into a shared team pool (ZG-0035). New server zip needed (net protocol 8)
builds.summary: NEEDS THE NEW SERVER ZIP: the net protocol went from 7 to 8, so a server from an older build refuses this client and this build refuses older servers. Download the server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release playtest/main-9671a83-2026-10-28 (Windows, includes the friends link script). Solo play needs nothing. What changed (completes M4): by day, harvesting resource nodes (E) feeds ONE shared team resource pool shown on the HUD (Team resources N, with how many you gathered); nothing spends it yet, building comes in M5. The DAY/NIGHT phase label moved to the top right so it no longer overlaps the info panel. The player no longer stalls when you push diagonally into a wall corner or a ramp channel (ported from Minecraft Clone). The night waves, melee and block from the last build are unchanged. Tower Defense building modules are in the code but not wired up yet.
builds.controls: Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, LEFT MOUSE ATTACKS, hold RIGHT MOUSE TO BLOCK, E HARVEST a resource node (or deposit drops at the Nexus), N calls a raid now (debug), Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. Server flags (after --): --day-s N / --night-s N (phase lengths in seconds), --debug-cycle (short 24 s + 16 s cycle), --day-length S, --seed N.
builds.test: By day, walk to the resource nodes and press E: does Team resources go up on the HUD, and does it show the same number for everyone in co-op (try two windows)? Is the DAY/NIGHT label at the top right and clear of the info panel? Push diagonally into the corner of the Nexus platform and up its ramps: do you keep moving? At night the waves, left click and right click block work as before. Use the new server zip: an older server shows a version mismatch message.

builds.title: Zeigote: night waves of alien enemies attack the Nexus (ZG-0034). New server zip needed (net protocol 7)
builds.summary: NEEDS THE NEW SERVER ZIP: the net protocol went from 6 to 7, so a server from an older build refuses this client and this build refuses older servers. Download the server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release playtest/main-a97d5b1-2026-10-28 (Windows, includes the friends link script). Solo play needs nothing. What changed (M4 phase B): at night, waves of Gears-style alien enemies spawn around each team's Nexus and walk to it and attack it; by day there are none. Left click attacks, right click blocks. Wave size grows with the night number and the number of players. At dawn leftovers dissolve and the Nexus repairs some health. If a team's Nexus is destroyed you get a NEXUS DESTROYED screen with a restart. The server clock from the last build (DAY and NIGHT) drives the waves.
builds.controls: Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, LEFT MOUSE ATTACKS, hold RIGHT MOUSE TO BLOCK, E harvest or deposit, N calls a raid now (debug, day or night), Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. Server flags (after --): --day-s N / --night-s N (phase lengths in seconds), --debug-cycle (short 24 s + 16 s cycle), --day-length S, --seed N.
builds.test: Wait for night (HUD shows NIGHT and a 'Night n: m Zeigote left' line). Do the aliens appear around the Nexus and walk to it? Does left click kill them, and does holding right click cut the damage you take? Do they damage the Nexus, and does it repair a little at dawn? Let the Nexus die: does the NEXUS DESTROYED screen come up and does restart work? Try co-op with two windows. Remember to use the new server zip: an older server shows a protocol mismatch message.

builds.title: Zeigote: server day/night cycle with DAY and NIGHT phases (ZG-0033). New server zip needed (net protocol 6)
builds.summary: The first step of day/night survival (M4 phase A). The server now runs a day/night clock with DAY and NIGHT phases and day numbers, the HUD shows the phase and a countdown to the next one, and the sky follows the phase (dark with stars at night); in co-op everyone sees the same phase at the same time. Also in this build, opt-in collision for the shared art kit (ZG-0031), which is off in Zeigote. NEEDS THE NEW SERVER ZIP: the net protocol went from 5 to 6, so a server from an older build refuses this client and this build refuses older servers. Download the server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release playtest/main-e809914-2026-10-28 (Windows, includes the friends link script). Solo play needs nothing.
builds.controls: No new controls. Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest or deposit, N next wave, Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. Server flags (after --): --seed N, --day-length S (whole cycle, split 60/40; 0 freezes it), --day-s N / --night-s N (phase lengths in seconds), --debug-cycle (a short 24 s + 16 s cycle).
builds.test: Watch the HUD: does it show DAY or NIGHT with the day number and a countdown to the next phase? Does the sky change when the phase changes (night is dark with stars)? In co-op with two browser windows, do both flip phase at the same time? Remember to use the new server zip: an older server shows a protocol mismatch message.

builds.title: Movement: smoothness pass (MV-0007)
builds.summary: A smoothness pass. Physics interpolation is on and the camera is interpolated every frame, so walking, sprinting, swinging and turning look smooth at any refresh rate. Crouch, slide and step transitions are eased instead of popping. New view effects: a small landing dip, a FOV boost at high speed and a slight roll when you strafe (all switchable off with view_effects=false). The rope now tightens over a few frames instead of yanking.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). Right mouse or Q fires and releases the grapple, hold E reels in, hold X reels out, Space releases. R respawns at the start with the view level, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Walk, sprint, swing and turn the camera: does it look smooth, with no micro-stutter or mouse lag (best on a 120/144 Hz monitor)? Crouch, stand up and start a slide: does the eye ease down and up with no pop? Land from a jump and from the tower: is the landing dip small and soft? Hook on while running away: does the rope tighten in a few frames rather than yank? Does the FOV widen a little as you swing fast, and the view lean a hair into a strafe? Is any of it too much or not enough? Anything still not smooth?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: player audio (VB-0028)
builds.summary: Sound for the first time. Footsteps depend on the ground (sand, grass, mud, rock, mudbrick ramps, water) and are faster when you sprint; there are jump and landing sounds, with a heavy thud after a fall of about 3 m or more; the axe, pickaxe and tree-fell and rock-break sounds, plus a pickup tick; a quiet desert wind all the time and a water bed near oases. Settings (O) has new Master volume and Sound effects sliders. In the browser sound starts after your first click or key. The web build also reports sound events in window.mcState (sfx_count, last_sfx, step_surface and more).
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day, Master volume, Sound effects); Esc releases the mouse.
builds.test: With sound on: walk and sprint on sand (crunchy steps, faster when sprinting, none when standing still, flying or pushing into a wall), then grass and mud at the oasis shore, wading into the water, a rock in the foothills, and up a ziggurat ramp (dull mudbrick knock). Jump, then drop off a ziggurat or hill: is the landing heavier the further you fall? Chop a palm with the axe (1) and break a rock with the pickaxe (2): hit sounds, then the finishing sound and the pickup tick. Is the desert wind pleasant and the oasis water audible? Open Settings (O): do the volume sliders work and stay after a reload? Tell us which sound is too loud, quiet, sharp or repetitive.

builds.title: Gears Clone: doubling waves, three alien types, gaits and telegraphed attacks
builds.summary: Waves now double each round (3, 6, 12, 24, 48), with at most 24 aliens alive at once and the rest streaming in from the far edges as you kill; a wave ends only when all are dead. There are three types: the normal violet alien, the small cyan skitterer (from wave 2) and the big orange brute (from wave 3). They move with distinct gaits (creep, trot, bound) and have four telegraphed attacks (claw swipe, bite lunge, tail stab, pounce) chosen by range. Aliens also slide round cover corners instead of standing stuck on them.
builds.controls: Click once to start (the first click starts the waves and captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, right mouse aims. Left mouse fires the current weapon. 1-4 or the wheel switches weapon, R reloads, C or Ctrl crouches, E takes or leaves cover. N or Enter calls the next wave now. Esc frees the mouse.
builds.notes: Click once to start. Press N or Enter to call the next wave early.
builds.test: Call a few waves with N: does the top of the screen count down (e.g. WAVE 5 - 48 ALIENS LEFT, 24 still to arrive) and does it stay playable with 24 alive? Watch the gaits: creep when searching, trot when circling, bound when chasing. Tell the three types apart (violet, cyan skitterer, orange brute) and react to each attack's telegraph. Do any aliens get stuck on cover?

builds.title: Movement: reeling keeps swing momentum (MV-0006)
builds.summary: Reeling in (hold E) or out (hold X) on the grapple now keeps your swing momentum. Reel-in keeps your sideways speed and adds a little (a shorter rope swings faster, like a real rope), and reel-out lets you drop on the rope smoothly with no snap. Reeling in hard to a short rope shouldn't fling you over the beam.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). Right mouse or Q fires and releases the grapple, hold E reels in, hold X reels out, Space releases. R respawns at the start with the view level, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Hook a beam or a tree branch, get a swing going, then hold E: does the swing speed up a little instead of stopping dead? Hold X mid-swing: do you drop smoothly with no jerk? Reel in hard to a short rope: are you whirled over the beam? Is the reel-in speed-up too little or too much?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: no more stall at the nexus core corner (VB-0027)
builds.summary: Fixes the stall when you walk at the nexus core's end corner (about 40-45 degrees toward the wall) from the ground in front of a ramp. If you are pinned against a corner or wall for 1.5 s you now slide off along it (expect a pause of about 1.4 s), and a second breaker frees you from creases where two surfaces meet. The nexus geometry is unchanged. The web build also exposes window.mcState (position, velocity, on_floor, on_wall, yaw and more, about 5 times a second) for testing.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse.
builds.test: From the ground in front of a nexus ramp, aim at the core's end corner (try turning 5 degrees at a time, 10 to 60 degrees toward the wall) and hold W: at about 40-45 degrees you may pause for about 1.4 s, then you should slide round the corner and never be held for good. Same while climbing, hugging the side wall up to the platform. Walking straight into a wall or the crystal still stops you.

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: no more stall at the ramp foot (VB-0026)
builds.summary: Fixes the nexus ramp stall: pressing W at the foot of a ramp while turned a little toward the wall or the low edge no longer leaves you standing still. You now slide along and climb on (the player's floor_block_on_wall is off). The crystal stops you the same distance (about 1.25 m) from its centre on every ramp.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse.
builds.test: Stand at the foot of a nexus ramp inside the channel, facing up but turned a little toward the wall or the edge, and hold W: do you slide along and climb on, never standing still? Try the toe, half way up and just below the top. Walking straight into the core wall should still stop you. Walk into the crystal from the platform: does it stop you at the same distance on every side of every nexus?

builds.title: Gears Clone: alien chitin hounds, click-to-start gate, ammo refills
builds.summary: The hounds are restyled as alien chitin quadrupeds: a smooth head with glowing green eyes, twitching hooked mandibles that flare when they notice you, segmented shell plates with back spikes, thin jointed insect legs with claws and a swaying tail. They flash magenta before a lunge and curl up when they die. Nothing runs until your first click: a CLICK TO START banner shows and no AI or waves start while you wait. You respawn with every weapon full, and a wave clear refills your ammo.
builds.controls: Click once to start (the first click starts the waves and captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, right mouse aims. Left mouse fires the current weapon. 1-4 or the wheel switches weapon, R reloads, C or Ctrl crouches, E takes or leaves cover. N or Enter calls the next wave now. Esc frees the mouse.
builds.test: Wait about 20 s before clicking: do the hounds stay still while the CLICK TO START banner shows? After the click, do they read as alien (eyes, mandibles, spiked shell, jointed legs, tail), walk, flash magenta before a lunge, and curl up on death? Empty the rifle and die: are you back at full ammo? Does a wave clear refill ammo? Balance is best judged on desktop.

builds.title: Movement: grove, tall pillars, lighter gravity, hookable surfaces (MV-0005)
builds.summary: Gravity is lighter (14.5, a 1.5 m jump with about 0.9 s in the air). South of the start is a grove of 18 tall trees (26-40 m) and six 30-45 m pillars to swing between. The hook now catches only on intended surfaces (trunks, branches, pillars, beams), never the ground, walls or rails. R respawns with the view level again. A pit with a red rim west of the ledges resets you, and the gap jumps are 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.5 / 6.0 m.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). Right mouse or Q fires and releases the grapple, hold E reels in, hold X reels out, Space releases. R respawns at the start with the view level, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Jump: floaty enough, or too floaty? Walk about 35 m south to the grove: does the ring turn green only on trunks, branches and pillars, and never on the ground? Hook the branch that points back at you, reel up with E, release and swing to the next tree. Walk into the red-rimmed pit west of the ledges: do you respawn at the start? Do the 4.5 and 6.0 m gaps need a sprint jump?

builds.title: Gears Clone: hounds (quadruped enemies), waves, player health
builds.summary: The practice dummies are replaced by hounds: four-legged enemies with a procedural gait that stalk, circle, flank and lunge in waves of 3, 5 and 7. You now have health (bar bottom left, red flash when bitten, regenerates after 5 s) and YOU DIED then respawn. The weapon bar is now top centre so the bow no longer overlaps it, and browser mouse look uses raw pointer movement scaled by the display scale.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't fire). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint. Right mouse aims down sights. Left mouse fires the current weapon (rifle hold, sword combo clicks, slingshot/bow hold and release). 1-4 or the wheel switches weapon, R reloads, C or Ctrl crouches, E takes or leaves cover, A/D slide along cover. N or Enter calls the next wave now. Esc frees the mouse.
builds.test: Hounds: do they read as four-legged and visibly walk, trot, circle and lunge (with a crouch telegraph)? Do hits flash and knock them back, big hits stagger, and do they fall and sink on death? Does the health bar show bottom left, and does dying show YOU DIED and respawn you? Is the weapon bar top centre with the bow clear of it? Does mouse look feel the same as on desktop? N/Enter calls the next wave. Balance is best judged on desktop.

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: solid, walkable nexus ziggurats (VB-0025)
builds.summary: The nexus ziggurats are solid now, with a walkable 2 m wide ramp up to the 5 m platform. You can walk or sprint up a ramp, walk round the crystal (it blocks you), step off the edge, and the side walls stop you. Trees and rocks no longer spawn inside or at the foot of a nexus. Fixes falling through the structure on the previous build.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch or the mouse wheel. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: Walk and sprint up a nexus ramp onto the platform, then round the crystal: do you ever fall through or snag at the bottom or top? Walk back down: any hops? Do the side walls stop you? Are there any trees or rocks at the ramp feet?

builds.title: Zeigote: slow co-op clients stay connected, DOWNED over Click to play, Nexus label clear of the HUD (ZG-0028-0030)
builds.summary: Co-op players on a slow computer (or several browser windows on one PC) no longer get dropped right after joining while the world builds, and a page that is still loading connects on the first try. If you are killed before clicking ‘Click to play’, the DOWNED screen now shows. The Nexus label no longer hides behind the info panel in small windows. Also art kit fixes shared with Minecraft Clone (ZG-0028) and an optional far Nexus beacon in the kit, off in Zeigote for now (ZG-0029). Co-op needs this build’s server (zeigote-server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release); servers from other builds are refused (net protocol 5).
builds.controls: No new controls. Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit at the Nexus, N next wave, Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. On the DOWNED screen: click Restart or Leave to menu, or press Esc for the menu. Server flags: --seed N, --time-of-day T (0..1), --day-length S (0 freezes the sky).
builds.test: Play co-op with two or more players (or two browser windows on one PC): does everyone stay connected for the whole session? Does a friend joining while their page is still loading get in first time? Is the Nexus label readable in a small window?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: far beacons as an art kit option, slimmer on web (VB-0023, VB-0024)
builds.summary: The far base beacons that cut through the daytime haze are now an art kit option shared with Zeigote. The browser build uses a slimmer variant: beacons widen up to 3 times with distance instead of 6. Also includes a terrain-height precision fix in the shared art kit (VB-0024); the terrain should look the same.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch or the mouse wheel. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: Fly high at 640 m in daylight: are the other bases’ beacons still easy to spot through the haze with the slimmer web beacons?

builds.title: Zeigote: DOWNED screen frees the mouse, first co-op connect works (ZG-0027)
builds.summary: Two fixes on top of the desert ring build. On the DOWNED (game over) screen the mouse is now free, so Restart and Leave to menu can be clicked, and Esc opens the menu from there. Joining co-op on a freshly opened page now connects on the first attempt instead of failing once while the game is still loading. Co-op needs this build’s server (zeigote-server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release); servers from other builds are refused (net protocol 5).
builds.controls: No new controls. Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit at the Nexus, N next wave, Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. On the DOWNED screen: click Restart or Leave to menu, or press Esc for the menu. Server flags: --seed N, --time-of-day T (0..1), --day-length S (0 freezes the sky).
builds.test: Let the Zeigote take the Nexus (or get downed): can you click Restart and Leave to menu straight away, and does Esc open the menu? In co-op, open a fresh page and Join: does it connect on the first try?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: clear spawn, visible beacons, sky phase names (VB-0022)
builds.summary: You now start on the open base pad facing the nexus and the oasis, instead of up against the ziggurat. The far base beacons cut through the daytime haze and get wider with distance, so you can spot other bases from the air. The Time of day slider names the sky phase (for example twilight). Also includes the art kit fixes shared with Zeigote.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch or the mouse wheel. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: At the start, are you on open ground facing the nexus and oasis? Fly high at 640 m in daylight: can you spot the other bases’ beacons through the haze? Drag Time of day: does the label name the phase (dawn, day, twilight, night)?

builds.title: Zeigote in the desert ring: art kit world and day/night sky (ZG-0026)
builds.summary: The game is now set in a desert ring of dunes, oases and boundary hills under a 10-minute day/night sky (visual only). Each team base sits on a flat sand pad, and the Nexus is a brick block with a glowing crystal, a light beam and braziers. In co-op the server picks the world seed, so everyone gets the same terrain. Players, Zeigote and pickups are still greybox. The browser uses a lighter look (224 m view, colours a little brighter than desktop). Co-op needs this build’s server (zeigote-server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release); older servers are refused (net protocol 5).
builds.controls: No new controls. Menu: Play Solo, Join Co-op, Host Co-op (desktop). In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit at the Nexus, N next wave, Esc menu (Leave to menu), V top-down view. Server flags: --seed N, --time-of-day T (0..1), --day-length S (0 freezes the sky).
builds.test: Does the desert ring look right: dunes, oases, hills at the edge, the brick Nexus with its crystal, beam and braziers? Watch the sky change over a few minutes. In co-op, do all players see the same terrain? Is anything hard to see at night?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: base ziggurats and shared art kit (VB-0020, VB-0021)
builds.summary: Each of the 6 bases now has a mudbrick ziggurat nexus 14 m in from the obelisk, with a glowing team-coloured crystal and a beacon you can see across the map. It is visual only for now, so you can walk through it. Terrain, props, water and sky now come from the shared ZgArt art kit and should look the same as before.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch or the mouse wheel. O opens Settings (render distance, time of day); Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: Find your base ziggurat next to the obelisk: does it read as your base up close? Fly high at 640 m, by day and at night (Time of day in Settings): can you spot the beacons of the other bases? Does anything else (terrain, water, sky, trees) look different from the previous build?

builds.title: Zeigote main menu: Play Solo, Host and Join Co-op (ZG-0023)
builds.summary: The game now opens on a main menu with Play Solo, Host Co-op (desktop only) and Join Co-op. Join takes a ws:// or wss:// address, a pasted https tunnel link, or host:port for ENet on desktop. It shows connecting, refused and failed states and lets you retry. Esc in the game offers Leave to menu (the host gets Stop hosting), so you can switch sessions without reloading. Links with ?server= still join automatically. Co-op needs this build’s server (zeigote-server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release); older servers are refused (net protocol 4).
builds.controls: Menu: click Play Solo, Join Co-op or Host Co-op (desktop). In Join: type or paste the address, Enter joins, R retries, Esc goes back. In game: click to lock the mouse, mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit, N next wave, Esc menu (Leave to menu / Stop hosting), V top-down view.
builds.test: Does the menu show, and does Play Solo start the game? Join Co-op with the server address: does it connect, and do you see the other players? Try a wrong address: does it say it failed, and does R retry? Leave to menu and join again without reloading. On desktop: Host Co-op and have a browser or second window join.

builds.title: Tower Defense: first-person nexus, Valheim/Rust-style snap building (branch preview)
builds.summary: Branch preview of the GDD v0.4 pivot (branch pivot/fps-nexus, not merged). First-person tower defense: defend a central nexus by building a maze. Building now works like Valheim and Rust: you hold a hammer, pieces snap onto the ground, on top of each other or beside each other, and the ghost turns green or red with a reason. Stability drops with each level and pieces are tinted blue, green, yellow or red in build mode. Walls stack at most 3 high, and removing a support collapses what it held, with a refund. You start on the nexus platform, which has ramps on its north and south sides.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse. WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold left mouse to shoot. B or Q toggles the hammer (build mode). 1-7 or the mouse wheel picks a piece: wall, long wall, gun tower, frost tower, foundation, floor, stairs. Left click places, R rotates, X or right click removes. N or Enter starts a wave. V overhead view, F4 flow arrows, F3 stats. Esc or P pauses, R restarts after the game ends.
builds.test: Stack walls: three are allowed and a fourth is refused with 'Too high'. Does a tower fit on top of a stack? Remove a lower wall: do the pieces above collapse and refund? Can you walk up player-built stairs and the nexus ramps? Is a build that would seal off the nexus refused? Does Start and Resume still capture the mouse?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: day/night cycle with torches (VB-0019)
builds.summary: A 12-minute day/night cycle with a sun and moon, a warm dusk, and a readable moonlit night with stars. Braziers mark each base and oasis. A new Torch (key 4) can be planted and picked back up, and the torch in your hand lights your way. Settings has a Time of day slider. The haze thins with altitude, and the holes and floating water seen from high up at long render distance are fixed. The web build uses a lighter look (at most 6 lights at once).
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn’t swing). Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt / 4 Torch or the mouse wheel. Torch: left mouse plants one where you aim, right mouse picks up the nearest. O opens Settings (render distance and time of day); Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: Drag Time of day in Settings (O) to dusk and night: is the night dark but readable? Do the braziers stand out as landmarks? Plant torches (4, left mouse), pick one back up, and walk into a cave holding a torch. At 640 m, fly high: any holes or floating water? On web, does it show when lights switch on and off (6 at most)?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: long-flight fixes and faster far hills (VB-0018)
builds.summary: Fixes for the browser crash after flying: terrain pieces are reused, so long flights are smoother and use less memory. At high render distance the far hills appear within a few seconds as a simplified pass, then sharpen nearest-first. Settings no longer opens over 'Click to play' on first load, the BENCH_MC console lines are gone, keys work on unusual keyboards, and a late mouse lock is handled.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't swing). Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly (Space up, Ctrl or C down). 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt or the mouse wheel. Hold left mouse to chop, break or dig; hold right mouse to raise ground (Sculpt). O opens Settings; Esc releases the mouse and shows Settings.
builds.test: Fly for a long time (F, then hold Shift), especially at 640 m render distance: does the browser still crash? If it does, note the browser, roughly how long you flew and what happened. At 640 m, do the boundary hills all round appear within a few seconds? On first load, is only 'Click to play' showing?

builds.ticket: sword combo, slingshot draw, bow repose
builds.title: Gears Clone: sword combo, slingshot draw, bow out of the way
builds.summary: The sword has a three-swing combo: slash right to left, slash back left to right, then a long stab. The slingshot pulls back before each shot (hold to draw, a quick tap lobs a weak pebble). The bow sits low on the left, clear of the crosshair. Clicking while a weapon isn't ready shows a RELOADING or LOADING note, and in the browser the hint says Esc only frees the mouse.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't fire). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint. Right mouse aims down sights (in cover: pops up). Left mouse: rifle hold to fire; sword click for the next combo swing (click again within about half a second, or hold, to chain); slingshot hold to draw, release to shoot; bow hold to draw, release to shoot. 1-4 or the wheel switches weapon, R reloads, C or Ctrl crouches, E takes or leaves cover, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse.
builds.test: Sword: do all three swings hit the practice dummy (behind you on the left), and does the rhythm feel right? Slingshot: does the meter fill while you hold, and does a quick tap lob a weak pebble? Is the bow out of the way of the crosshair, idle and drawing? Click during a reload: do you see the orange note?

builds.title: Movement: lighter feel, walled course and grappling hook (MV-0003, MV-0004)
builds.summary: Lighter feel: walk 4.3 and sprint 7.0 m/s, a 1.3 m jump and a bit more air control. The course now has border walls, rails on the slide-slope tops, and you respawn if you fall below it. Mouse look is fixed for high-DPI screens. New grappling hook: a grapple park about 50 m east of the start with pillars and beams, an overhang over a gap and a grapple-only tower. The crosshair ring turns green when a target is in range.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). Right mouse or Q fires and releases the grapple, hold E reels in, hold X reels out, Space releases. R respawns at the start, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Does it feel lighter but still grounded? Do the walls stop you at the edge? At the grapple park (east), does the ring turn green on a beam, and can you swing from beam to beam, reel up to the grapple-only tower and land on top? Does the swing feel weighty but fun?

builds.title: Movement: web fixes, one-click start and Space jump (MV-0002)
builds.summary: Web playtest fixes. One click on Start or Resume now captures the mouse and plays. Space jumps in the browser. The start screen sits on a solid panel below the START sign, and the key hint moved to the bottom-right, clear of the Back to builds badge.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). R respawns at the start, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Does one click on Start and on Resume put you straight into the game? Does Space jump, and can you jump onto the 50 cm step? Crouch through the tunnel. Is a slide down the slide slopes faster than one on flat ground? Does it feel heavy enough, or too sluggish?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone: render distance setting and far-terrain detail (VB-0017)
builds.summary: O or Esc opens Settings with a Render distance slider from 48 to 640 m. Your choice is saved, and the web default is 128 m. Far terrain is simplified and gains detail as you get closer. The warm cave light now reaches into the tunnels.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't swing). Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt or the mouse wheel. Hold left mouse to chop, break or dig; hold right mouse to raise ground (Sculpt). Esc releases the mouse. O opens Settings (Esc also opens them).
builds.test: Open Settings (O) and move the Render distance slider, for example to 320 or 640 m: does the view reach further? Reload the page: is your setting kept? At 640 m from the hills, can you see the whole ring, and how much does FPS drop? Walk into a cave at the foot of the hills: is the warm light there?

builds.title: Gears Clone: first-person conversion
builds.summary: Gears Clone is now first person. You see the weapon in your hands, and right-click aims down the sights. In cover you crouch, then pop up or lean out to shoot. The rifle, sword, slingshot and bow each have their own animations.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't fire). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint. Right mouse aims down sights (in cover: pops up). Left mouse fires: hold for the rifle's auto fire, the sword swings, the slingshot fires per click, and the bow holds to draw and releases to shoot. 1-4 or the wheel switches weapon, R reloads, C or Ctrl crouches, E takes or leaves cover, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse.
builds.test: Can you see each of the 4 weapons in your hands, and does each have its own animation? Does right-click aim down the sights? In cover, does right-click pop you up to shoot over it, and do shots hit the dummy instead of your cover? Does the capture click leave your ammo unchanged?

builds.title: Movement m0: first-person controller and test course (MV-0001)
builds.summary: A first-person movement test course, aiming for grounded, weighty movement rather than snappy arcade movement. Walk and sprint build up and bleed off speed, the jump is about 1 m, and sprinting then holding C slides on momentum, picking up speed downhill. The course has ramps, steps, a crouch tunnel, jump gaps, slide slopes and ledges.
builds.controls: Click to start (captures the mouse). Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold C to crouch (sprint + C slides). R respawns at the start, F1 shows or hides the debug HUD. Esc frees the mouse and pauses; click to resume.
builds.test: Does the movement feel heavy enough, or too sluggish? Jump: about 1 m, little air steering. Ramps up to 40 degrees walkable, 50 too steep? Steps: 15 and 30 cm walk up, 50 cm needs a jump? Crouch through the tunnel. Gaps: walking clears about 2.5 m, sprinting about 3.5 m? Slide: about 5 m on flat, faster down the slide slopes?

builds.title: Tower Defense: first-person nexus pivot, pointer-lock fix (branch preview)
builds.summary: Branch preview of the GDD v0.2 pivot (branch pivot/fps-nexus, not merged). Fixes Start and Resume on the web: one click now captures the mouse and plays instead of landing back on the pause menu. First person: defend a central nexus against enemies from four gates by building walls and towers into a maze they reroute through live, and shoot them with a hitscan gun.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold left mouse to shoot. B or Q toggles build mode, 1-4 picks a piece, R rotates, left mouse places, X or right mouse sells. N or Enter starts a wave. V overhead view, F4 flow arrows, F3 stats. Esc or P pauses (Resume recaptures the mouse). R restarts after game over.
builds.test: Does the title click capture the mouse, does Esc pause, and does Resume recapture? In build mode, is the ghost green/red with a reason, and does selling refund? Do enemies really walk around your walls (V and F4 help)? Is sealing the nexus refused? Does the gun feel useful next to the towers?

builds.title: Minecraft Clone M4: ring desert map (VB-0015)
builds.summary: A new map: a 10,000 BC Mesopotamian desert ring of dunes, date palms, acacias, rocks and oases, with steep hills and caves all round so you never see the edge. The axe chops trees for wood and the pickaxe breaks rocks for stone (counters top right). Holding a button now keeps repeating even at low FPS (VB-0016). The world takes a few seconds to build on the web, and FPS is lower than before (about 38k triangles).
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't swing). Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. 1 Axe / 2 Pickaxe / 3 Sculpt or the mouse wheel. Hold left mouse to chop, break or dig; hold right mouse to raise ground (Sculpt). Esc releases the mouse.
builds.test: Chop a palm (4 hits) or acacia (5) with the axe and break a rock (3 hits) with the pickaxe: do the wood and stone counters rise? Does holding the button keep repeating? Walk outward: do the hills hide the edge of the map, and can you walk into a cave? Wade into the oasis in front of you.

builds.title: Tower Defense: first-person nexus pivot (branch preview)
builds.summary: Branch preview of the GDD v0.2 pivot (branch pivot/fps-nexus, not merged). First person: defend a central nexus against enemies coming from four gates. Build walls and towers into a maze that they reroute through live, and shoot them with a hitscan gun.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, hold left mouse to shoot. B or Q toggles build mode, 1-4 picks a piece, R rotates, left mouse places, X or right mouse sells. N or Enter starts a wave. V overhead view, F4 flow arrows, F3 stats. Esc or P pauses (Resume recaptures the mouse). R restarts after game over.
builds.test: Does the title click capture the mouse, does Esc pause, and does Resume recapture? In build mode, is the ghost green/red with a reason, and does selling refund? Do enemies really walk around your walls (V and F4 help)? Is sealing the nexus refused? Does the gun feel useful next to the towers?

builds.title: Gears Clone: four weapons
builds.summary: Four weapons now: the rifle, a sword with a visible slash, a slingshot that lobs pebbles, and a bow you hold to draw and release (a full draw takes a dummy down in one arrow). Switch with 1-4 or the mouse wheel. A practice dummy by the start is there for the sword.
builds.controls: WASD move, mouse look, click to capture the mouse (doesn't fire). Left mouse fires the rifle, swings the sword, shoots the slingshot, or hold to draw the bow and release to shoot. Right mouse aims, R reloads, 1-4 or the mouse wheel switches weapon, Esc frees the mouse.
builds.test: Does each weapon hit a dummy (watch the hits counter)? Sword: turn around, the practice dummy is behind you on the left. Slingshot: does the pebble arc onto the crosshair? Bow: does the draw meter show, and does a full draw take a dummy down in one arrow? Does the wheel switch weapons without grabbing the mouse? Esc frees the mouse and nothing freezes.

builds.title: Zeigote co-op player tags (ZG-0025)
builds.summary: Each co-op player now has a number (P1-P4), its own body colour and a 'P#' tag above its head, and the HUD shows 'You are P#'. Other players move smoothly (100 ms interpolation). A tab left in the background stays connected and catches up when shown again. To play together, start this build's server (zeigote-server zip from the Zeigote-Godot release) and use the Server address field on the Zeigote page.
builds.controls: No new controls. Click to start and lock the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit, N calls the next wave, Esc/P menu (online it doesn't pause the world), R restart (online: restarts the match for everyone), V top-down debug view.
builds.test: Co-op: does every player have a different colour and a P# tag, and does the HUD say 'You are P#'? Do other players move smoothly? Put a tab in the background for half a minute, then come back: is it still connected and caught up? Also: a different build is refused with a version-mismatch message.

builds.title: Zeigote co-op fixes (ZG-0024)
builds.summary: Co-op players now spawn side by side facing the Nexus, and every new group starts with a full Nexus (the server resets the match when the last player leaves, which caused the 0/1000 OVERRUN). Joining retries automatically (15 s per attempt, 4 attempts) and shows RETRYING. The solo DOWNED screen shows only 'No respawn'. At low FPS the camera no longer overshoots and hit flashes always show. To join a server, put ?server=ws://127.0.0.1:9080 before the # in the URL: https://janxzs.github.io/playtest-builds/?server=ws%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A9080#main-e69816b-2026-10-24 (the server must be this same build).
builds.controls: Click to start and lock the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit, N calls the next wave, Esc/P menu (online it doesn't pause the world), R restart (online: restarts the match for everyone), V top-down debug view. One PC, several players: one browser window each, side by side, not tabs.
builds.test: Co-op: do players spawn side by side, does every new group start with a full Nexus, and does a failed join retry by itself (RETRYING)? Solo: does DOWNED show only 'No respawn'? Low FPS: does the camera stay steady and do hit flashes show? Also: shared deposits, tier and waves, and a mismatch message for a different build.

builds.title: Minecraft Clone M3: smooth Valheim-style terrain (VB-0014)
builds.summary: The block world is gone. It's now smooth Valheim-style terrain with meadows, rolling hills and rock cliffs, grass and rock blended by slope, a procedural sky, fog and warm sunlight. You can dig and build up the ground with a soft brush. On the web expect a 4.5-7 s load and about 5-8 FPS on a software renderer.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (the first click doesn't dig). Hold left mouse to dig and hold right mouse to raise a soft 1.5 m sphere (repeats every 0.12 s; a preview sphere shows where it lands). WASD move, Space jump, Shift sprint, F fly. Esc releases the mouse and never quits.
builds.test: Dig and raise quickly, including across section borders (every 16 m in x/z and at heights 16/32/48): no cracks, holes or flickering seams. Walk up and down slopes: hills up to ~45 degrees are walkable, steeper cliffs block you, no bouncing downhill or snagging on invisible edges. Dig a crater and walk in and out; raise a mound and stand on it. Look: grass on flat ground, rock on steep slopes, brown dirt where you edited, soft fog in the distance. On web the world builds in over a few seconds. Terrain tris ~24.9k in the top-left label at start.

builds.title: Zeigote online co-op for up to 4 players (ZG-0022)
builds.summary: Up to 4 players co-op on one team with a shared Nexus. Teammates show shield and attack poses, movement is predicted, and the HUD shows players n/4 and ping. While connecting it says 'If your browser asks, click Allow'. Players spawn 12 m in front of the Nexus, facing it. Without ?server= it's the same solo game. To join a server, put ?server=ws://127.0.0.1:9080 before the # in the URL, e.g. https://janxzs.github.io/playtest-builds/?server=ws%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A9080#main-bbdb15b-2026-10-24 (the server must be this same build).
builds.controls: Click to start and lock the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block, E harvest/deposit, N calls the next wave, Esc/P menu (online it doesn't pause the world), R restart (online: restarts the match for everyone), V top-down debug view. One PC, several players: one browser window each, side by side, not tabs.
builds.test: Solo: same loop as before. Co-op: does everyone connect (click Allow if the browser asks), see players n/4 and a ping, and see teammates with shield and attack poses? Does movement feel responsive? Do deposits, tier and waves stay shared? Does a 5th player get 'server full' and a different build get a version-mismatch message? Does R on game over restart the match for everyone?

builds.title: Gears Clone: web camera fix at low FPS
builds.summary: Fixes the black shape and the sky-only view (camera smoothing blew up below ~10 FPS). On load you see the arena, cover, dummies and the player from behind. The first click only captures the mouse and no longer fires. Each shot shows a visible muzzle flash plus yellow tracers.
builds.controls: Click the game to capture the mouse (that click doesn't fire). WASD move, Shift sprint, hold right mouse to aim (pops you up out of cover), hold left mouse to fire, R reload, C/Ctrl crouch, E snap to cover or leave it, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse; click the game to recapture.
builds.test: On load you should see the arena, cover, dummies and the player from behind, not just sky, and the click that captures the mouse should not fire. Also: muzzle flash and yellow tracers on each shot, hits from cover (E, then hold right mouse and fire), sparks and scorch marks, and any stutter on the first shot.

builds.title: Minecraft Clone M2: lighter meshing, no load freeze (VB-0003)
builds.summary: Same terrain drawn with about a third of the triangles. On the web the world fills in over about 2 s instead of freezing at load, and Esc no longer kills the page. Known gap: occasional ~9 ms frames from the no-threads mesher.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse (that click doesn't edit). Mouse look, WASD/arrows move, Space jump, Shift sprint, LMB break, RMB place plank, F toggles fly (Space/Ctrl move up and down). Esc releases the mouse; click to recapture.
builds.test: Break and place blocks quickly, including on chunk borders (every 16 blocks) and at height 16: edits should appear within a frame or two, with no holes, missing or doubled faces. After load the world should fill in nearest-first over ~2 s with no gaps. Terrain tris ~7.0k in the top-left label at start. Press F and fly around: no gaps or flickering between merged faces.

builds.title: Gears Clone: visible rifle and projectile bullets
builds.summary: The player now holds a visible rifle, and each shot shows a muzzle flash and a yellow tracer bullet that flies to the crosshair, with sparks and scorch marks on walls. Popping out of cover to aim now hits the dummy instead of your own cover.
builds.controls: Click the game to capture the mouse. WASD move, Shift sprint, hold right mouse to aim (pops you up out of cover), hold left mouse to fire, R reload, C/Ctrl crouch, E snap to cover or leave it, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse; click the game to recapture.
builds.test: Is the rifle visible and held right (low when walking, raised when aiming, muzzle-up in cover, lower when crouched)? Does firing show a muzzle flash and yellow tracers to the crosshair, with hits landing a moment later? From cover (E), hold right mouse and fire at a dummy: do shots hit the dummy, not your cover? Do wall and floor hits leave a spark and a fading scorch mark? Does hip fire turn you to the crosshair? Any stutter on the first shot or low frame rate. Known: firing low in cover without aiming hits your own cover (no blind fire yet).

builds.title: Zeigote in first person: jump and shield block (ZG-0021)
builds.summary: Zeigote is now first person. Click to start (the click locks the mouse), Space to jump, left click to attack, and hold right click to raise a shield that blocks most damage from the front. Game over now waits about 1 s and only restarts with R or the Restart button.
builds.controls: Click to start and lock the mouse. Mouse look, WASD move, Space jump, left mouse attacks, hold right mouse to block (slower, no attacks), E harvest/deposit, N calls the next wave, Esc/P pause, R restart, V top-down debug view.
builds.test: Does the start click lock the mouse cleanly, and does Esc free it and pause? Does blocking a Zeigote hit feel readable (shield up, 'Blocked!', blue flash), and is the jump height OK? Does the ~1 s game-over delay stop accidental restarts? Do the Zeigote come for you within ~8 m and do the hits feel fair? Wave pacing, stuck spots, HUD overlap and performance.

builds.title: Tower Defense M1: first playable build
builds.summary: A 3D greybox tower defense. Build Gun, Cannon and Frost towers beside the path, then upgrade, sell and retarget them to survive 20 waves of Grunts, fast Runners and armored Brutes.
builds.controls: Click to start. 1-3 or the build bar picks a tower; LMB places or selects, RMB cancels; U upgrade, X sell, Tab cycle targeting; N, Enter or Space starts the next wave; F speed 1x/2x/3x; P pause; WASD, arrows or middle-drag pan; wheel zoom; F3 stats; Esc pause menu.
builds.test: Does the title click start the game without placing a tower? Building: the ghost turns green/red, the range ring shows, money goes down. Select a tower: do Upgrade, Sell and Target (and U / X / Tab) work? Waves: Runners rush at the end, Brutes shrug off Gun hits; are Cannons and Frost useful? Is it too easy? Do camera pan and zoom feel OK, and do the Esc menu's Resume and Restart work? Known: balance not tuned, no sound, greybox only.

builds.title: Gears Clone M0: web fixes
builds.summary: The game no longer grabs the mouse on load (click once to capture it), and in the browser Esc only frees the mouse and never quits, so the freeze is gone. Gameplay is unchanged.
builds.controls: Click the game to capture the mouse. WASD move, Shift sprint, hold right mouse to aim, hold left mouse to fire, R reload, C/Ctrl crouch, E snap to cover or leave it, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse; click the game to recapture.
builds.test: Does the shoulder camera and aiming feel responsive? Does snapping to cover with E, sliding along it and popping out to aim feel right? Do hits on the orange dummies register where the crosshair is (known issue: shots can hit your own cover just in front of you, fix coming next)? Any stutter or low frame rate in the browser.

builds.title: Gears Clone M0: standalone extract
builds.summary: A greybox third-person cover shooter with a shoulder camera, aiming, automatic hitscan fire with reloads, crouch, and snap-to-cover with sliding along it, against respawning orange target dummies.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse. WASD move, Shift sprint, hold RMB to aim, hold LMB to fire, R reload, C/Ctrl crouch, E snap to cover or leave it, A/D slide along cover. Esc frees the mouse; don't press it a second time in the browser (it quits and freezes the game, use Back to builds instead).
builds.test: Does the shoulder camera and aiming feel responsive? Does snapping to cover with E, sliding along it and popping out to aim feel right? Do hits on the orange dummies register where the crosshair is (known: shots can hit your own cover just in front of you)? Any stutter or low frame rate in the browser.

builds.title: Zeigote: enemies hunt you + first-person view (ZG-0019, ZG-0020)
builds.summary: Zeigote now chase and attack you within about 8 m, with a red hit flash, HP loss, feed lines and downed/respawn in normal play. The Nexus label is large and readable again, and there's an optional first-person view.
builds.controls: Click the title to start. WASD/arrows move, Space or left mouse attacks (where you look in first person), E deposits at the Nexus or harvests resource nodes, N calls the next wave, V toggles first person (click to lock the mouse; Esc or losing the lock releases it and pauses), P/Esc pauses, R restarts. Top-down is the default.
builds.test: First person (V): does pointer lock grab and release cleanly in your browser, and is aiming melee at the crosshair readable? Do the Zeigote come for you within about 8 m, and do the hits feel fair (wind-up, red flash)? Wave pacing, Tier 2 reachability, stuck spots, HUD overlap and performance.

builds.title: Minecraft Clone M0 baseline
builds.summary: A small 64×64-block world with grass hills you can walk around, break blocks in and build on with planks. FPS and remesh stats show top-left.
builds.controls: Click to capture the mouse and look. WASD/arrows move, Space jump, Shift sprint, left mouse breaks a block, right mouse places a plank. Esc quits (in the browser use Back to builds instead).
builds.test: Does walking, jumping and looking feel right? Do breaking and placing blocks hit the block under the crosshair? Watch the FPS and remesh numbers top-left while you edit, and report stutter.

builds.title: Zeigote solo thin slice: playtest fixes
builds.summary: Same solo loop as the last build, with fixes: clicking the title now starts the game (without attacking), pause and game-over screens have Resume/Restart buttons, and the Nexus label no longer covers the HUD.
builds.controls: Click the title to start. WASD/arrows move, Space or left mouse attacks, E deposits at the Nexus or harvests brown resource nodes, N calls the next wave, P/Esc pauses, R restarts (or use the Resume/Restart buttons).
builds.test: Is the loop clear without instructions? Do movement, attack and the camera feel OK in the browser? Wave pacing and whether Tier 2 (100 drops) is reachable. Report stuck spots, stacking enemies, unreachable pickups, HUD overlap and performance.

builds.title: Zeigote solo thin slice (M3 basic)
builds.summary: First playable loop, solo and offline: collect glowing Zeigote drops, deposit them at the teal Nexus to reach Tier 1, then fight off the Zeigote waves that follow and bank what they drop.
builds.controls: Click the game first. WASD/arrows move, Space or left mouse attacks, E deposits at the Nexus or harvests brown resource nodes, N calls the next wave, P/Esc pauses, R restarts.
builds.test: Is the loop clear without instructions? Do movement, attack and the camera feel OK in the browser? Wave pacing and whether Tier 2 (100 drops) is reachable. Report stuck spots, stacking enemies, unreachable pickups, HUD overlap and performance.

builds.title: Zeigote foundation (M0)
builds.summary: Greybox foundation scene: the team Nexus on a ground plane. Single-player only in the browser; no controls yet.
builds.controls: No controls yet (static scene).
builds.test: Boots and renders in your browser.
